macro_context: Nightly pass after the post-election rotation; full evidence in journal/research/2026-11-04-dossier.md. The overnight blue-wave drop reversed before the open and the S&P closed +1.58% (Dow +3.0%, equal weight at a record), but as a rotation: financials, staples, health care, discretionary and homebuilders up 3-7%, megacap platforms AAPL/MSFT/AMZN +5-7%, while AI suppliers (SOX -3.1%, MU -7%), Texas power (VST -13.8%), neoclouds (CRWV -9.9%), defense (LMT -6.9%) and energy (WTI -8.3% on Vance blaming the Iran war) fell. SPX dealer gamma turned positive in our snapshot and the vendor's (flip 7,669), which bears on the index, not the spread. One idea tonight, at confidence 1 because the base rate's analogs are all down days and today was an up-day rotation; bounces in the policy-hit baskets themselves show no edge in our history (coin flips). After-hours movers into the open: APP +20%, COHR +7%, QCOM -6%, ARM -2%. After our exit: NET, IREN, LITE, MCHP, ABNB earnings; Friday's October payrolls at 08:30 (+59-65k) is the main risk to anyone carrying beyond the close.

ideas.thesis: High beta against low vol is washed out after a policy shock that the market traded as a rotation. SPHB/SPLV fell 2.8% today and 10.4% in five days (20-day -23.0%, z50 -2.15, RSI 34), while SPLV closed at a 52-week high with RSI 74. In our bars, a day of -2.5% or worse with the five-day spread at -8% or worse was followed by an open-to-close gain 10 of 11 times (mean about +185 bp; declustered 7 of 7), and the edge is not market beta: SPY's next open-to-close averaged about zero on those days. Positioning backs a bounce: hedge funds cut net leverage at the fastest pace in months (GS prime book, October -4.2 pp) and gross exposure the most since 2016 (MS), CTAs are short, and VIX fell 20% to 16.6, back in contango. The big caveat, and why confidence is 1: every one of those 11 cases came on a down day for SPY (-0.5% to -4.9%); today SPY rose 1.65%. On the five days in our history when SPY rose while the spread fell 2% or more, the next session lost 4 times (mean -77 bp), including Jul 24 and Jul 28 2026 in this cycle's momentum crash. Today's selloff was a policy repricing (Texas governor, Democratic Congress, defense budget), which can extend a factor trend rather than reverse it. Research and technicals agree the high-beta side is washed out; the analog that matches today's up-day rotation argues against the bounce.
ideas.invalidation: The SPHB/SPLV spread is down more than 1.5% from the open (about 0.75 of its 203 bp daily standard deviation), SPHB trades below 132.00 (-3.1% from Wednesday's 136.18 close, about 0.9 ATR), or SPY trades below 760.00.
